expectations.text: All three models (User, Post, Comment) are extracted into detected-entities.json as separate entries
expectations.evidence: detected-entities.json entities array has 3 entries: class_name='User' (line 6), class_name='Post' (line 18), class_name='Comment' (line 34) — one per `model` block in fixtures/prisma/schema.prisma.

expectations.text: Each entity's table_name matches the @@map(...) value in the fixture (e.g., User → 'users', Post → 'posts', Comment → 'comments')
expectations.evidence: Fixture: User has @@map("users"), Post has @@map("posts"), Comment has @@map("comments"). detected-entities.json: User.table_name='users' (line 7), Post.table_name='posts' (line 19), Comment.table_name='comments' (line 35). All three @@map values picked up via the per-class windowing pass.

expectations.text: Every @relation(fields: [...], references: [...]) field produces a relationship in detected-entities.json with a non-empty target_entity that names another extracted model — no blank target_entity strings
expectations.evidence: Fixture has two @relation declarations: `author User @relation(...)` on Post and `post Post @relation(...)` on Comment. detected-entities.json: Post.relationships[0].target_entity='User' (line 25, type many_to_one) and Comment.relationships[0].target_entity='Post' (line 41, type many_to_one). Both targets non-empty and reference extracted models. The Prisma profile's `\b\w+\s+([A-Z]\w*)\s+@relation\b` pattern captured the type token before the marker.

expectations.text: One-to-many sides (e.g., posts Post[]) produce relationships of type one_to_many; their corresponding many-to-one inverse (e.g., author User @relation(...)) produces type many_to_one, both with the correct target_entity
expectations.evidence: Fixture User has `posts Post[]` → detected-entities.json User.relationships[0]={type:'one_to_many', target_entity:'Post'} (lines 12-13). Fixture Post has `author User @relation` → Post.relationships[0]={type:'many_to_one', target_entity:'User'} (lines 24-25). Fixture Post has `comments Comment[]` → Post.relationships[1]={type:'one_to_many', target_entity:'Comment'} (lines 28-29). Fixture Comment has `post Post @relation` → Comment.relationships[0]={type:'many_to_one', target_entity:'Post'} (lines 40-41). All four pairs captured with correct type + target.

expectations.text: Generated database-mapping.md frontmatter has type='entity' and orm_profile='prisma'
expectations.evidence: database-mapping.md line 3 (`type: entity`) and line 6 (`orm_profile: prisma`).

expectations.text: Mermaid erDiagram contains nodes named 'users', 'posts', 'comments' (the table names from @@map, not the model names) and at least one edge of cardinality ||--o{ linking users-posts AND another linking posts-comments
expectations.evidence: database-mapping.md Mermaid block lines 23-26: `erDiagram\n    users ||--o{ posts : ""\n    posts ||--o{ comments : ""`. Node names 'users', 'posts', 'comments' all appear as edge endpoints (Mermaid implicitly declares entities from edges). Required edges both present: users ||--o{ posts AND posts ||--o{ comments. The bidirectional canonicalization in output.ts (A2) collapsed the User↔Post pair to the one_to_many side as expected.

expectations.text: mermaid_lint.js reports no issues on the generated page
expectations.evidence: Ran `node skills/doc-wiki/scripts/mermaid_lint.js --page <database-mapping.md>` — exit 0, output `[]`. Captured in mermaid-lint.txt.

eval_feedback.overall: Prisma detection extracted all 3 models, mapped each to its @@map table name, captured every @relation with the correct one_to_many / many_to_one type and target_entity (the profile's capture-group-based pattern dereferenced correctly to User/Post/Comment), and rendered a clean Mermaid diagram with the two required ||--o{ edges.
